Technical SEO.title: Google Aggregator and Supplier Units Gain Things To Do Query Support
Technical SEO.summary: Google has updated its aggregator unit and supplier unit help documentation to include support for Things To Do queries. This structured-result type is not new in Google Search, but has now been formally added to both unit help docs, making it relevant for travel and activity-based enterprise sites.

Digital Marketing / Martech.title: Tripadvisor Says SEO Will Still Weigh On Growth In 2027
Digital Marketing / Martech.summary: Tripadvisor linked a writedown largely to search changes and expects SEO headwinds to continue weighing on its growth through next year, while noting that marketing now consumes a greater share of its revenue. This is a direct signal for enterprise travel SEO teams tracking how algorithm and AI search shifts affect major OTA business models.

Digital Marketing / Martech.title: Ziff Davis Says Organic Google Referrals Fell About 37%
Digital Marketing / Martech.summary: Large publisher Ziff Davis reported that organic Google referrals fell approximately 37%, with the company pointing to Search Console's AI report as part of its analysis. The story highlights the growing measurable impact of AI-driven search changes on enterprise content publishers.

Digital Marketing / Martech.title: Cloudflare CEO Likens AI Agent Optimization To A New Version Of SEO
Digital Marketing / Martech.summary: Cloudflare's CEO described AI agent optimization as a new form of SEO, noting that OpenAI pays for signals that inform its crawler when pages change, and that sites may offer agents reduced costs when they disclose the purpose of their visits. This has direct implications for how enterprise sites manage crawl access and GEO strategy.

AI Search / GEO.title: We Opted Out of Google AI Search - Here's What Happened
AI Search / GEO.summary: A site tested opting out of Google's AI features to measure the traffic contribution of AI Overviews and AI Mode, finding an estimated 21% of its clicks were attributable to those AI surfaces. The experiment also suggested a possible lift on regular listings when AI features are removed, offering rare empirical data for GEO strategy decisions.

AI Search / GEO.title: Google's AI Features Sent One Site An Estimated 21% Of Its Clicks
AI Search / GEO.summary: By opting out of Google's AI features, one site was able to estimate that AI Overviews and AI Mode collectively drove approximately 21% of its clicks, with potential uplift observed on standard organic listings. This is one of the first documented attempts to quantify AI-surface traffic contribution, making it highly actionable for enterprise GEO planning.
